headline: Netherlands wasteful, Japan steal a point from chaos
story: Netherlands commanded Dallas with 55% possession and a suffocating press (2.0 high-press phases, forcing 33 turnovers), but squandered a gilt-edged 36th-minute chance. Japan, reduced to 37% possession and dawdling recovery times of 22.3 seconds, surrendered territory at will. Yet the match pivoted on clinical finishing: Gravenberch and van Dijk's dominance at midfield and rear went unrewarded when low-probability strikes found the net—Netherlands' second goal arrived from just 0.02 xG at the 64th mark. Japan, seemingly overwhelmed, equalised twice: first from chaos at 57', then Nakamura's composed defence cracked when a 0.14 xG chance sailed past at 89'.

The numbers tell a damning story for Ronald Koeman. Netherlands' 0.63 xG return of two goals masked the 36th-minute miss (0.17 xG)—had Summerville or another converted there, the shape changed entirely. Japan's arithmetic was equally peculiar: 0.34 xG became two goals, a variance that Keito Nakamura (7.8 rating) absorbed through positioning rather than perfect marking. The pace of this match, driven by Netherlands' ball-recovery speed (14.2 seconds versus Japan's laboured 22.3), suggested control. Instead, both sides finished as if playing with eyes closed. Japan's 3-4-2-1 never imposed threat but lasted through Daichi Kamada's workrate in midfield, whilst van Dijk's 7.9 rating went unmolested until chaos opened late.

keyMoment.text: Japan's late equaliser from 0.14 xG, a chance materialised from defensive frailty

home.verdict: Dominance squandered; clinical finishing must improve immediately.
points: Miss the 36' sitter (0.17 xG) and you don't control the scoreline—higher standards required
Score twice from 0.63 xG yet concede from 0.34; the 2.0 high-press phases justify intensity, not complacency
Gravenberch's 8.0 rating means midfield mastery; ensure forwards are equally sharp

away.verdict: Resilient but can't bank on 0.34 xG returning two goals again.
points: 22.3-second recovery under 55% possession is unsustainable; sharper pressing reduces their workload
Nakamura's 7.8 rating held the line despite chaos—but relying on defensive heroics rather than shape is perilous
Late chances (0.14 xG) won't always arrive at 89'; need to generate threats earlier

statLine: Japan converted twice from 0.34 expected goals, whilst Netherlands' 0.63 xG yield produced two goals and one glaring miss—a study in finishing variance.
